```{r libraries}
library(knitr)
```

```{r read_tables}
csv_dir <- file.path("csv", "RUN_nov11")
figure_dir <- file.path("figures", "RUN_nov11")
.read <- function(name){
  utils::read.csv(file.path(csv_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
results_df <- .read("results")
experiment_df <- .read("experiments")
score_df <- .read("scores")
block_df <- .read("blocks")
validity_df <- .read("validity")

fmt <- function(x, digits = 4){formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f")}

# One line of a summary block, as a number.
.block <- function(key, split, rule){
  bool_vec <- block_df$key == key & block_df$split == split &
    block_df$rule == rule
  stopifnot(sum(bool_vec) == 1)
  as.numeric(block_df$value[bool_vec])
}

# One column of one experiment's row.
.experiment <- function(number, column){
  experiment_df[[column]][experiment_df$experiment == number]
}
.commit <- function(number){paste0("`", .experiment(number, "commit"), "`")}

# Per-example scores of one rule on one split, in the order of the ids.
.scores <- function(split, rule){
  sub_df <- score_df[score_df$split == split & score_df$rule == rule, ]
  sub_df[order(sub_df$id), ]
}

# Mean score of one rule in one stratum.
.stratum <- function(split, rule, factor_name, level){
  sub_df <- .scores(split, rule)
  mean(sub_df$score[as.character(sub_df[[factor_name]]) == level])
}

# The paired comparison of `donor_wls` with `raw_null`, per split.
paired_list <- lapply(c(dev = "dev", test = "test"), function(split){
  baseline_df <- .scores(split, "raw_null")
  best_df <- .scores(split, "donor_wls")
  stopifnot(all(baseline_df$id == best_df$id))
  difference_vec <- best_df$score - baseline_df$score
  list(difference = mean(difference_vec),
       num_examples = length(difference_vec),
       num_improved = sum(difference_vec < 0),
       range = range(difference_vec),
       se = stats::sd(difference_vec) / sqrt(length(difference_vec)))
})

kept_df <- experiment_df[experiment_df$outcome == "kept", ]
withdrawn_df <- experiment_df[experiment_df$outcome == "withdrawn", ]
discarded_df <- experiment_df[experiment_df$outcome == "discarded", ]
# Every `keep` row of the log is in one of the two tables of kept commits.
stopifnot(nrow(kept_df) + nrow(withdrawn_df) ==
            sum(results_df$status[-1] == "keep"),
          nrow(kept_df) + nrow(withdrawn_df) + nrow(discarded_df) ==
            nrow(experiment_df))

num_experiments <- nrow(experiment_df)
best_commit <- kept_df$commit[nrow(kept_df)]
total_gain <- results_df$score[1] - .block("score", "dev", "donor_wls")
large_vec <- c(5, 7, 12)
large_gain_vec <- -vapply(large_vec, .experiment, numeric(1),
                          column = "delta")
flat_df <- kept_df[kept_df$experiment > 13, ]
```

# Overview {-}

This document is built from the design memo of the loop (`MEMO_claude.md`),
the record of the bank as built (`BANK.md`), the run report that the
autoresearch protocol requires (`RUN_nov11_claude.md`), and the tables of
the run (`csv/RUN_nov11/`). It follows the sections of that protocol's run
report, and every number in its prose is read from those tables.

**The question.** Version 1.2.0 of eSVD2 reports a log fold change and a
standard error whose ratio is not a usable Wald statistic. The autoresearch
loop searched for a rule that reports, from one fitted cohort, a log2 fold
change that is unbiased at every effect size and a standard error that is
the sampling SD of that log fold change. The run `nov11` edited one file
(`report_rule_claude.R`) over `r num_experiments` experiments, each scored
on a fixed bank of simulated cohorts.

The document argues five things.

1. The kept rule, `donor_wls`, is a donor-level weighted regression of log
   pseudobulk ratios with a moderated residual variance (Section 1.3).
2. It scores `r fmt(.block("score", "dev", "donor_wls"))` on the dev split
   and `r fmt(.block("score", "test", "donor_wls"))` on the held-out test
   split, against `r fmt(.block("score", "dev", "raw_null"))` and
   `r fmt(.block("score", "test", "raw_null"))` for the baseline `raw_null`,
   and the dev gain carried to test in full (Section 3).
3. Three of the `r nrow(kept_df)` kept commits carry
   `r round(100 * sum(large_gain_vec) / total_gain)`% of the dev gain
   (Section 4).
4. Two commits that passed the keep rule were withdrawn, because their
   standard error followed the estimated log fold change, which the score
   rewards and the gate does not detect (Section 5).
5. Quantities of the fit that are estimated at the level of cells (the
   case-control coefficient, the low-rank term, the nuisance rate) did not
   help (Section 6).

*How to read.* A green box closes each results section with what that
section changes. The blue box describes the simulated bank once, and a grey
box opens each section that reuses it. The orange box in Section 8 is the
procedure. A reader of the boxes alone gets the argument.

| Stage | What it does | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Definitions | notation, the four rules by name, the score and the gate | 1 |
| The run | branch, budget, what stopped it, the bank | 2 |
| Result | dev and test blocks against the baseline | 3 |
| Attribution | every kept commit, every withdrawn one, every discarded one | 4, 5, 6 |
| Constants | each numeric constant of the rule with its reason | 7 |
| Recommendation | the procedure, and what is left to decide | 8 |

# Definitions

## Notation

A cohort has cells $c$, genes $g = 1, \dots, p$ and donors
$d = 1, \dots, n$, of which $n_1$ are cases and $n_0$ controls. $A_{cg}$ is
the count of cell $c$ and gene $g$. $\ell_{cg}$ is the fitted library size
of eSVD-DE, which holds every fitted covariate effect except the
case-control one, the gene intercept included. $\beta_g$ is the true log2
fold change of gene $g$, and a rule reports the pair
$(\widehat\beta_g, s_g)$ in log2 units.

A rule is a function `report_lfc_se(view)`. The list `view` holds what a
user has after `eSVD()`: the counts, the design matrix, the donor and the
arm of each cell, the fitted library, the posterior mean and variance, and
the nuisance rate.

| Name in the tables | Rule | Reads | Defined in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `raw_null` | log ratio of the arms' mean donor ratios, delta-method SE, shifted and rescaled by the empirical null | counts, fitted library | 1.2 |
| `donor_wls` | arm coefficient of a donor-level weighted regression of log pseudobulk ratios, moderated residual variance, constant shift | counts, fitted library, design | 1.3 |
| `gap_trend` | `donor_wls` as of experiment 27, with the variance moderated toward a trend in the arithmetic-geometric gap of the donor ratios | counts, fitted library, design | 5 |
| `deseq2` | DESeq2 on donor pseudobulk counts, stored with the bank as a reference | counts | 1.4 |

## The baseline: `raw_null`

With $m_{dg}$ the mean of $A_{cg} / \ell_{cg}$ over the cells of donor $d$,
$M_{1g}, M_{0g}$ the arm means of $m_{dg}$ and $V_{1g}, V_{0g}$ the sample
variances of $m_{dg}$ within each arm,

$$\widehat\beta^{\,\text{raw}}_g = \log_2\frac{M_{1g}}{M_{0g}}, \qquad
s^{\text{raw}}_g = \frac{1}{\ln 2}\sqrt{\frac{V_{1g}}{n_1 M_{1g}^2} + \frac{V_{0g}}{n_0 M_{0g}^2}}.$$

With $(\delta_0, \sigma_0)$ the mean and SD of the empirical null fitted to
$\widehat\beta^{\,\text{raw}}_g / s^{\text{raw}}_g$ over the genes,
`raw_null` reports
$(\widehat\beta^{\,\text{raw}}_g - \delta_0 s^{\text{raw}}_g,\; \sigma_0 s^{\text{raw}}_g)$.

## The kept rule: `donor_wls`

1. *Donor summary.* With $y_{dg} = \sum_{c \in d} A_{cg}$ and
   $L_{dg} = \sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}$,
   $$l_{dg} = \log\frac{y_{dg} + 1/2}{L_{dg}}.$$
2. *Design.* $D$ is the $n \times q$ donor-level matrix whose columns are
   the intercept, the arm indicator, and every column of the fit's design
   that is constant within donors, reduced to full rank.
3. *Donor offsets.* With $r_{dg}$ the residuals of the least-squares
   regression of $l_{\cdot g}$ on $D$, the offset of donor $d$ is
   $o_d = \text{median}_g\, r_{dg}$, and $l_{dg} \leftarrow l_{dg} - o_d$.
   The regression is repeated, which gives the fitted values $f_{dg}$ and
   the residuals $r_{dg}$.
4. *Precision weights.* With $\mu_{dg} = L_{dg}\, e^{f_{dg}}$ the expected
   count, the two constants of
   $$\text{Var}(l_{dg}) = \tau^2 + \frac{\phi}{\mu_{dg}}$$
   are fitted by least squares of $r_{dg}^2\, n / (n - q)$ on
   $1 / \mu_{dg}$ over all donors and genes, each floored at 0, and
   $w_{dg} = 1 / (\tau^2 + \phi / \mu_{dg})$.
5. *Weighted regression.* With $W_g = \text{diag}(w_{\cdot g})$,
   $$\widehat\theta_g = (D^\top W_g D)^{-1} D^\top W_g\, l_{\cdot g}, \qquad
   a_g = \big[(D^\top W_g D)^{-1}\big]_{\text{arm}}, \qquad
   S_g = \frac{1}{n - q}\sum_d w_{dg}\,(l_{dg} - D_d^\top \widehat\theta_g)^2 .$$
   The vector $\widehat\theta_g$ has one entry per column of $D$, and
   $\widehat\theta_{g,\text{arm}}$ is its entry for the arm indicator: the
   difference between cases and controls in the mean of $l_{dg}$, at equal
   donor-level covariates, in natural-log units. It is computed by this
   regression and is not eSVD-DE's fitted case-control coefficient
   $\widehat z_{g,\text{cc}}$ (Section 1.3.1).
6. *Moderated variance.* A smoothing spline $t(\cdot)$, with its
   smoothness chosen by generalized cross-validation, is fitted to
   $\log S_g$ against $x_g = \tfrac1n \sum_d f_{dg}$. With $\nu = n - q$,
   $\psi$ the digamma function and $\psi'$ the trigamma function, the prior
   degrees of freedom $\nu_0$ solve
   $$\psi'(\nu_0 / 2) = \text{mean}_g\,\{\log S_g - t(x_g)\}^2 - \psi'(\nu / 2),$$
   the prior variance is
   $\log S_{0g} = t(x_g) - \psi(\nu/2) + \log(\nu/2) + \psi(\nu_0/2) - \log(\nu_0/2)$,
   and
   $$\widetilde S_g = \frac{\nu_0 S_{0g} + \nu S_g}{\nu_0 + \nu}.$$
   When the right-hand side of the equation for $\nu_0$ is not positive,
   $\nu_0 = \infty$ and
   $\widetilde S_g = \exp\{t(x_g) - \psi(\nu/2) + \log(\nu/2)\}$.
7. *The pair before centring.*
   $$\widehat\beta^{\,0}_g = \frac{\widehat\theta_{g,\text{arm}}}{\ln 2}, \qquad
   s_g = \frac{\sqrt{\widetilde S_g\, a_g}}{\ln 2}.$$
8. *Centring.* With $\delta_0$ the mean of the empirical null fitted by
   `eSVD2::multtest()` to $z_g = \widehat\beta^{\,0}_g / s_g$,
   $$\widehat\beta_g = \widehat\beta^{\,0}_g - \delta_0 \cdot \text{median}_g\, s_g .$$
   The rule reports $(\widehat\beta_g, s_g)$, and the SD of the empirical
   null is not used.

Four things changed against `raw_null`. The donor summary is a ratio of
sums on the log scale. The estimator is a regression that adjusts again for
the donor-level covariates and weights donors by their precision. The
variance is pooled over the arms and moderated across genes, with the cost
of the covariates in $a_g$ and in $\nu$. The centring is one constant per
cohort, with no rescaling of the SE. Steps 5 to 7 are the moderated
statistic of limma on precision weights in the manner of voom
(`smyth2004linear`, `law2014voom`), applied to eSVD-DE's fitted library in
place of a normalized library size.

### Where the eSVD-DE fit enters

eSVD-DE fits, for cell $c$ and gene $g$, the mean count

$$\widehat{\mathbb{E}}[A_{cg}] = \exp\Big(\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g + \sum_{k} \widehat z_{gk}\, C_{ck}\Big)
= \underbrace{\exp\Big(\sum_{k \ne \text{cc}} \widehat z_{gk}\, C_{ck}\Big)}_{\ell_{cg}}
\cdot \exp\big(\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g + \widehat z_{g,\text{cc}}\, C_{c,\text{cc}}\big),$$

where $C_{ck}$ is covariate $k$ of cell $c$ (the intercept, the log of the
cell's total count, the case-control indicator cc, and any others),
$\widehat z_{gk}$ is the fitted coefficient of gene $g$ on covariate $k$,
and $\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g$ is the fitted low-rank term. The
fitted library $\ell_{cg}$ is the first factor, floored at 0.1 as
`compute_posterior()` floors it. It is the count the fit expects from cell
$c$ for gene $g$ at the cell's depth and covariates, before the arm and
the low-rank term act.

**`donor_wls` uses one fitted quantity, $\ell_{cg}$, and uses it in two
steps, both times summed over the cells of a donor,
$L_{dg} = \sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}$.**

- **Step 1, as the denominator of the donor summary.** The count of a cell
  has mean $\ell_{cg} \lambda_{cg}$, with $\lambda_{cg}$ the cell's
  expression relative to its library, so
  $$\mathbb{E}[y_{dg}] = \sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}\, \lambda_{cg}
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \frac{y_{dg}}{L_{dg}} \approx \frac{\sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}\, \lambda_{cg}}{\sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}},$$
  the library-weighted mean of $\lambda_{cg}$ over the donor's cells. The
  response of the regression, $l_{dg} = \log\{(y_{dg} + 1/2) / L_{dg}\}$,
  is the log of that ratio. This step is where the fit's adjustment for
  depth and for every covariate other than the arm, cell by cell and gene
  by gene, enters the log fold change. A pseudobulk method divides by one
  normalized library size per donor in this place.
- **Step 4, in the expected count that sets the weights.** The expected
  count $\mu_{dg} = L_{dg}\, e^{f_{dg}}$ multiplies the summed fitted
  library by the donor regression's own fitted ratio, and the weight
  $w_{dg} = 1 / (\tau^2 + \phi / \mu_{dg})$ falls as $\mu_{dg}$ falls.
  Through the weights $L_{dg}$ also enters $\widehat\theta_g$, $a_g$ and
  $S_g$ of step 5.

Every later quantity inherits the fit through these two steps only. The
$f_{dg}$ of steps 3, 4 and 6 are fitted values of the donor-level
regression of $l_{dg}$ on $D$. They are computed by the rule and are not
values of the eSVD-DE fit.

| Quantity of the eSVD-DE fit | Used by `donor_wls` | Where |
|---|---|---|
| fitted library $\ell_{cg}$, from $\widehat z_{gk}$ for $k \ne \text{cc}$ | yes | steps 1 and 4, as $L_{dg}$ |
| design matrix $C$ (built by `format_covariates()`, not fitted) | yes | step 2, its columns that are constant within donors |
| case-control coefficient $\widehat z_{g,\text{cc}}$ | no | the arm effect is estimated again in step 5 |
| low-rank term $\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g$ | no | |
| nuisance rate $\widehat\gamma_g$ and its capped status | no | |
| posterior mean and variance of each cell and gene | no | |

The donor-level covariates therefore act twice: once inside $\ell_{cg}$,
where the fit removes their effect cell by cell, and once in $D$, where
the regression of step 5 removes what is left of them between donors and
charges the arm coefficient for it through $a_g$ and $\nu$. The call to
`eSVD2::multtest()` in step 8 uses a function of the package on the rule's
own $z_g$ and reads nothing of the fit. Experiments 11, 18 and 24 tried
the three unused fitted quantities in turn, and each lost (Section 6).

### The logic of the estimate, and what remains of eSVD-DE

**The short answer.** `donor_wls` computes its log fold change and its SE
from the counts and the fitted library alone. The embedding, the fitted
case-control coefficient, the nuisance rate, the posterior mean and the
posterior variance do not enter either number. The rule is close to a
limma-voom analysis of donor pseudobulk counts in which eSVD-DE's fitted
library replaces the normalized library size.

**The log fold change.** The target is the log2 ratio of mean expression
between the arms at equal depth and equal covariates, and the unit that is
replicated is the donor. The rule therefore reduces each donor to one
number per gene, $l_{dg}$, the log of the donor's expression relative to
its fitted library (Section 1.3.1), and compares the arms on that scale.
With no donor-level covariate and equal weights, step 5 reduces to a
difference of two averages,

$$\widehat\theta_{g,\text{arm}} = \frac{1}{n_1}\sum_{d\,\in\,\text{cases}} l_{dg} \;-\; \frac{1}{n_0}\sum_{d\,\in\,\text{controls}} l_{dg},
\qquad \widehat\beta^{\,0}_g = \frac{\widehat\theta_{g,\text{arm}}}{\ln 2}.$$

The regression generalizes this difference in two ways: the columns of $D$
for sex and age hold those covariates equal between the arms, and the
weights $w_{dg}$ let a donor with few counts for the gene count for less.

**The standard error.** If $l_{dg}$ has variance $\sigma_g^2 / w_{dg}$
around its regression line, independently over donors, then

$$\text{Var}\big(\widehat\theta_{g,\text{arm}}\big) = \sigma_g^2\, a_g,
\qquad a_g = \big[(D^\top W_g D)^{-1}\big]_{\text{arm}}
\;\overset{\text{no covariates, equal weights}}{=}\; \frac{1}{n_1} + \frac{1}{n_0}.$$

The factor $a_g$ is known from the design, and it grows when sex or age is
unbalanced between the arms. The variance $\sigma_g^2$ is the spread of the
donors around the line, donor-to-donor biological variation plus the
sampling noise of the counts, and $S_g$ estimates it from $n - q$ degrees
of freedom. With 10 donors that estimate is too noisy to use gene by gene,
so step 6 replaces it by $\widetilde S_g$, a weighted average of $S_g$ and
the value that genes of similar expression have. The SE is
$\sqrt{\widetilde S_g\, a_g} / \ln 2$. It is a between-donor SE, and no
within-donor or posterior variance is added to it.

**Why the other fitted quantities are not used.** Each was tried, in the
exploration of 2026-11-07 or in this run.

| Fitted quantity | What happened when it was used | Why |
|---|---|---|
| posterior mean | the between-donor SE of posterior donor means was 0.65 to 0.73 times the SD of the log fold change over replicate cohorts (exploration) | the posterior mean of a cell is $w\, A_{cg} / \ell_{cg} + (1 - w) \times \text{fit}$, with $w = \ell_{cg} / (\ell_{cg} + \widehat\gamma_g)$, so it pulls donors toward the fit and toward each other, and their spread understates the noise by about $w$ |
| posterior variance | as the SE of version 1.2.0, 3.4 to 5 times that SD (exploration); as a within-donor term added to the between-donor variance, kept at experiment 8 and removed at experiment 15 | it describes the uncertainty of a cell's expression given the fit, and the error of the log fold change is dominated by which donors were sampled |
| case-control coefficient $\widehat z_{g,\text{cc}}$ | experiment 11, worse by `r fmt(.experiment(11, "delta"), 3)` nats | it is fitted over cells, so a donor with many cells counts for more, and experiment 10 shows that weighting donors by cell count alone costs `r fmt(.experiment(10, "delta"), 3)` nats |
| embedding $\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g$ | experiment 18, worse by `r fmt(.experiment(18, "delta"), 3)` nats | in a cohort of 10 to 40 donors the low-rank term absorbs part of the donor effects, so dividing by it removes variation that the error of the log fold change still contains |
| nuisance rate $\widehat\gamma_g$ | experiments 24 and 35, worse by `r fmt(.experiment(24, "delta"), 3)` and `r fmt(.experiment(35, "delta"), 4)` nats | the gene's level already predicts its variance, and the rate is capped for part of the genes |

The baseline `raw_null` had already dropped the posterior mean and
variance for the first two reasons, before the run began. The run then
found no fitted quantity worth adding back.

**What the run does not show.** Two limits bear on how far this result
reaches.

- The run did not score `donor_wls` with a plain library size (the cell's
  total count) in place of $\ell_{cg}$. The share of the
  `r fmt(-.block("score_vs_deseq2", "test", "donor_wls"), 3)` nats over
  `deseq2` that the fitted library contributes, as opposed to the weights
  and the moderation, is therefore not measured.
- The bank draws each cell's embedding independently of its donor and its
  arm, so the low-rank term has no difference in cell state between cases
  and controls to remove. A cohort in which cell state is confounded with
  the arm is the setting where the embedding is expected to matter, and
  the bank does not contain it.

**The p-value.** The p-value was not on trial, and nothing in the package
changed. Two p-values exist after this run, and they use the fit
differently.

| Statistic | Computed by | Uses of the eSVD-DE fit |
|---|---|---|
| the package's p-value | `compute_test_statistic()` and `compute_pvalue()`, unchanged | posterior mean and posterior variance of every cell, hence the embedding, every coefficient and the nuisance rate; then the empirical null |
| the Wald statistic $\widehat\beta_g / s_g$ of `donor_wls` | `report_lfc_se()` | the fitted library only |

A user who reports the log fold change and SE of `donor_wls` beside the
package's p-value reports two analyses of the same counts, and the two can
disagree on a gene. Whether `compute_log_fold_change()` should adopt
`donor_wls`, and whether the p-value should then follow it, are decisions
for Section 8.

The implementation is `RULE_nov11_claude.R`, which mirrors commit
`r paste0("\x60", best_commit, "\x60")` and needs no other file of the
project. Its code follows.

```{r rule_code, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE, code=readLines("RULE_nov11_claude.R")}
```

## The score, the gate and the reference

The score of one fitted cohort is the Gaussian negative log-likelihood of
the truth under the reported pair, in nats per gene,

$$\text{NLL} = \frac{1}{p}\sum_{g=1}^{p}\left[\tfrac12 \log\!\left(2\pi s_g^2\right) + \frac{(\widehat\beta_g - \beta_g)^2}{2 s_g^2}\right],$$

and lower is better. One example of the bank is a pair of cohorts, the
score of an example is the mean of its two cohorts' NLL, and the score of a
rule is the mean over the examples of a split. In expectation the NLL of a
gene is smallest when $s_g^2$ equals the mean squared error of
$\widehat\beta_g$, so it charges an SE that is too large, an SE that is too
small, a biased log fold change and a noisy one in the same unit.

A proper score rewards shrinkage toward zero wherever the truth is sparse.
The gate therefore requires `slope_weak`, the slope of the reported log
fold change on the truth over the weak genes ($0 < |\beta_g| < 0.5$), to
lie in $[0.9, 1.1]$, and a commit that fails the gate is not kept.

A commit is kept when its paired gain over the best commit so far is
positive and at least one paired standard error over the
`r paired_list$dev$num_examples` dev examples. `deseq2` is scored with the
same formula on the pair that DESeq2 reports from donor pseudobulk counts,
and the line `score_vs_deseq2` is a rule's score minus that reference.

# The run

| | |
|---|---|
| Branch | `autoresearch_lfcse/nov11`, cut from `2026-11-07_std` at `r paste0("\x60", results_df$commit[1], "\x60")` |
| Budget agreed at setup | 40 experiments or 4 hours, with 8 cores for a scoring |
| Experiments run | `r num_experiments`, from `r results_df$time[1]` to `r results_df$time[nrow(results_df)]` |
| By status | `r nrow(kept_df)` kept, `r nrow(withdrawn_df)` kept and then withdrawn, `r nrow(discarded_df)` discarded |
| Wall-clock per scoring | `r fmt(min(results_df$seconds), 0)` to `r fmt(max(results_df$seconds), 0)` seconds |
| Best commit | `r paste0("\x60", best_commit, "\x60")` (experiment `r kept_df$experiment[nrow(kept_df)]`) |

**What stopped the run.** The run was stopped by a decision at experiment
`r num_experiments`, two short of the budget. The
`r nrow(flat_df)` commits kept after experiment 13 moved the dev score by
`r fmt(-sum(flat_df$delta))` nats in total, and the ideas left were weaker
than the ones just discarded.

**One departure from the protocol.** Experiments
`r paste(withdrawn_df$experiment, collapse = " and ")`
(`r paste0("\x60", withdrawn_df$commit, "\x60", collapse = ", ")`) passed
the keep rule and were withdrawn afterwards (Section 5). The branch was
reset to the previous kept commit `r .commit(27)`, the best-score files
were rebuilt from a fresh scoring of that commit, and the two commits are
preserved on the branch `autoresearch_lfcse/nov11-gap-invalid`. The
protocol has no such step, so the withdrawal is Kevin's to confirm.

Two experiments crashed on coding errors (a formula interface and a
string that the scorer's tripwire refuses). Both were fixed and amended
before they were logged, so the log has no `crash` row.

::: {.generator}
The bank `lfcse-bank-1` holds `r paired_list$dev$num_examples` dev and
`r paired_list$test$num_examples` test examples. An example is a pair of
cohorts of 600 genes whose counts follow the eSVD model at rank 3, with
donor random effects on the log scale, and each cohort is fitted end to end
by eSVD2 1.2.0. The case-control effects of the two cohorts are correlated
at 0.8 with a size ratio of 2. Six factors are crossed, one example per
cell and split: the number of donors (10, 20, 40, half per arm), the cells
per donor (50 for every donor, or unequal from 30 to 600), the range of the
true Gamma rate (narrow, wide), the effects (`sparse`: 10% of genes
nonzero; `sparse_up`: the same sizes, all positive; `dense`: every gene
nonzero), the covariates (none, or donor-level sex and age with sex
imbalanced 60/40 between the arms), and the donor SD (0.2, 0.5, the
quartiles estimated on the Velmeshev cohort). Both arms share the donor SD.
The truth of an example is the generator's case-control coefficient in log2
units. `BANK.md` records the bank as built.
:::

# Dev and test against the baseline

::: {.reuse}
The bank of Section 2. `donor_wls` was scored on the test split once, after
the run ended; `raw_null` was scored on both splits when the bank was
built.
:::

```{r block_table}
key_vec <- c("score", "score_se", "rmse", "coverage_95", "z_sd_null",
             "bias_null", "slope_weak", "wald_false", "rho_err",
             "score_vs_deseq2")
stratum_key_vec <- grep("^score_(donors|cells|rates|effects|covariates|donor_sd|status)",
                        unique(block_df$key), value = TRUE)
.block_column <- function(split, rule){
  vapply(c(key_vec, stratum_key_vec), function(key){
    fmt(.block(key, split, rule))
  }, character(1))
}
block_table_df <- data.frame(
  line = c(key_vec, stratum_key_vec),
  baseline_dev = .block_column("dev", "raw_null"),
  baseline_test = .block_column("test", "raw_null"),
  best_dev = .block_column("dev", "donor_wls"),
  best_test = .block_column("test", "donor_wls"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(block_table_df, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Line of the block", "`raw_null`, dev",
                           "`raw_null`, test", "`donor_wls`, dev",
                           "`donor_wls`, test"),
             align = "lrrrr",
             caption = "Table 1. The scorer's summary block of the baseline and of the best commit on both splits. Scores are in nats per gene and lower is better; all four blocks pass the gate.")
```

```{r paired_table}
paired_table_df <- data.frame(
  split = names(paired_list),
  gain = vapply(paired_list, function(x){fmt(x$difference)}, character(1)),
  se = vapply(paired_list, function(x){fmt(x$se)}, character(1)),
  ratio = vapply(paired_list, function(x){fmt(-x$difference / x$se, 0)},
                 character(1)),
  improved = vapply(paired_list, function(x){
    paste0(x$num_improved, " of ", x$num_examples)
  }, character(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(paired_table_df, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Split", "`donor_wls` minus `raw_null`",
                           "Paired SE", "Gain in paired SE",
                           "Examples improved"),
             align = "lrrrr",
             caption = "Table 2. The paired comparison over the examples of each split.")
```

The gain is `r fmt(-paired_list$dev$difference)` nats per gene on dev and
`r fmt(-paired_list$test$difference)` on test, so the run did not fit the
dev bank. `deseq2`, which `raw_null` trailed by
`r fmt(.block("score_vs_deseq2", "dev", "raw_null"), 3)` nats on dev, now
trails `donor_wls` by
`r fmt(-.block("score_vs_deseq2", "dev", "donor_wls"), 3)` on dev and
`r fmt(-.block("score_vs_deseq2", "test", "donor_wls"), 3)` on test. On
test the coverage of $\widehat\beta_g \pm 1.96\, s_g$ is
`r fmt(.block("coverage_95", "test", "donor_wls"), 3)` and the SD of
$\widehat\beta_g / s_g$ over the exactly null genes is
`r fmt(.block("z_sd_null", "test", "donor_wls"), 2)`. The number of
Benjamini-Hochberg discoveries at level 0.05 per 100 exactly null genes,
`wald_false`, fell from
`r fmt(.block("wald_false", "test", "raw_null"), 2)` to
`r fmt(.block("wald_false", "test", "donor_wls"), 2)`.

```{r fig_strata, out.width="95%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 1. Mean score per stratum with one standard error, `raw_null` (grey) beside `donor_wls` (blue), on the dev and the test split."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "strata.png"))
```

`donor_wls` is below `raw_null` in every stratum of both splits. The gain
is largest at 10 donors, where the test score moved from
`r fmt(.stratum("test", "raw_null", "donors", "10"), 3)` to
`r fmt(.stratum("test", "donor_wls", "donors", "10"), 3)`, and with unequal
cells per donor
(`r fmt(.stratum("test", "raw_null", "cells", "unequal"), 3)` to
`r fmt(.stratum("test", "donor_wls", "cells", "unequal"), 3)`).

```{r fig_paired, out.width="85%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 2. The difference `donor_wls` minus `raw_null` for each test example, sorted, colored by the number of donors and the covariates."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "paired.png"))
```

Every test example improved, by `r fmt(-paired_list$test$range[2], 2)` to
`r fmt(-paired_list$test$range[1], 2)` nats per gene, and the largest
improvements are the 10-donor cohorts with sex and age in the design.

::: {.takeaway}
`donor_wls` improves on `raw_null` by
`r fmt(-paired_list$test$difference, 3)` nats per gene on held-out
examples, `r fmt(-paired_list$test$difference / paired_list$test$se, 0)`
paired standard errors, in every one of the
`r paired_list$test$num_examples` examples and every stratum. Its Wald
statistic is calibrated on this bank (null SD
`r fmt(.block("z_sd_null", "test", "donor_wls"), 2)`, coverage
`r fmt(.block("coverage_95", "test", "donor_wls"), 3)`), and it is ahead of
DESeq2's pseudobulk pair by
`r fmt(-.block("score_vs_deseq2", "test", "donor_wls"), 3)` nats.
:::

# What helped

::: {.reuse}
The bank of Section 2, dev split. The gain of a commit is against the best
commit at the time, computed from scores logged to four digits.
:::

```{r fig_trajectory, out.width="85%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 3. The dev score of every experiment in order: kept commits filled, discarded ones open, the two withdrawn commits as crosses. Dashed lines mark the baseline and the final best."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "trajectory.png"))
```

```{r kept_table}
.experiment_table <- function(sub_df, sign){
  data.frame(
    experiment = sub_df$experiment,
    commit = paste0("`", sub_df$commit, "`"),
    direction = sub_df$direction,
    idea = sub_df$idea,
    change = ifelse(is.na(sub_df$paired_se),
                    fmt(sign * sub_df$delta),
                    paste0(fmt(sign * sub_df$delta), " (",
                           fmt(sub_df$paired_se), ")")),
    strata = sub_df$strata,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
knitr::kable(.experiment_table(kept_df, sign = -1), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("#", "Commit", "Direction", "Idea",
                           "Gain (paired SE)", "Strata that moved"),
             align = "llllrl",
             caption = "Table 3. Every kept commit in order, dev split. Directions are the memo's: D1 the donor summary, D2 the variance form, D3 the centring, D4 borrowing across genes, D5 using more of the fit.")
```

Three commits carry
`r round(100 * sum(large_gain_vec) / total_gain)`% of the dev gain of
`r fmt(total_gain)` nats.

- **The moderation (experiment 5, `r fmt(large_gain_vec[1], 3)` nats).** A
  variance estimated from 5 to 20 donors per arm is stabilized by the other
  genes' variances, and the gain is in every stratum.
- **The design factor (experiment 7, `r fmt(large_gain_vec[2], 3)` nats).**
  The SD of the empirical null had been compensating for two separate
  things: the degrees of freedom and the variance inflation that
  donor-level covariates cost, which $a_g$ and $\nu$ now charge directly,
  and true weak effects, which had been inflating the null SD in the
  `dense` cells.
- **The log-scale estimator (experiment 12, `r fmt(large_gain_vec[3], 3)`
  nats).** The mean of log donor means is more efficient than the log of
  the mean because the bank's donor effects are log-normal. This gain is
  the only large one that comes from the log fold change (the RMSE fell)
  and not from the SE.

The remaining kept commits are small. Experiments 8 and 15 cancel: the
stored within-donor term acted as a general widening while the coverage was
0.944 and became redundant once the regression variance was in place.
Experiments 9, 27 and 31 are each at about one paired SE, the level at
which the keep rule admits a change with no effect about one time in six.
Experiment 27 (the donor offset of step 3) is weakly tested by this bank,
whose donors carry almost no depth error common to all genes.

```{r fig_chosen, out.width="85%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 4. The median standard error reported per test example, `donor_wls` against `raw_null`, by donor SD and covariates; the grey line marks equality."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "chosen.png"))
```

The median SE of `donor_wls` is at or below that of `raw_null` in nearly
every test example and varies less between examples of the same donor
count, which is the effect of the moderation and of the removal of the
cohort-wide null-SD factor.

::: {.takeaway}
The gain comes from how the variance is estimated and from the scale of the
donor summary, in three steps: moderating the per-gene variance across
genes, charging the donor-level covariates through the regression in place
of the empirical null's SD, and estimating the log fold change on the log
scale. The other `r nrow(kept_df) - length(large_vec)` kept commits add
`r fmt(total_gain - sum(large_gain_vec), 3)` nats together, and several of
them are within the noise that the keep rule admits.
:::

# The withdrawn commits

::: {.reuse}
The bank of Section 2, dev split. The SE diagnostics below were computed
during the run on `r validity_df$num_cohorts[1]` dev cohorts by a script
that was not kept, and are recorded in `csv/RUN_nov11/validity.csv`.
:::

```{r withdrawn_table}
knitr::kable(.experiment_table(withdrawn_df, sign = -1), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("#", "Commit", "Direction", "Idea", "Gain",
                           "Strata that moved"),
             align = "llllrl",
             caption = "Table 4. The two commits that passed the keep rule and were withdrawn (`gap_trend`).")
```

`gap_trend` moderated the variance toward a trend in the gap between the
log arithmetic mean and the mean log of a gene's donor ratios, and it
scored `r fmt(.experiment(29, "score"))` against
`r fmt(.experiment(27, "score"))` for the commit before it. The gap is
computed over all donors before the regression, so it contains the
between-arm sum of squares, which is the squared estimated log fold change.
With that covariate the prior degrees of freedom were infinite in every
cohort checked, and the SE became a smooth function of the gap.

```{r validity_table}
knitr::kable(validity_df[, c("rule", "commit", "se_ratio", "spearman")],
             row.names = FALSE, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Rule", "Commit",
                           "Median SE, strong-effect genes over the others",
                           "Spearman correlation of SE and absolute logFC"),
             caption = "Table 5. Whether the reported SE follows the estimate, on 12 dev cohorts.")
```

Under `gap_trend` the SE of strong-effect genes was
`r fmt(validity_df$se_ratio[1], 2)` times that of the other genes. The
score rewards an SE that grows with the estimate because most true effects
in the bank are near zero, so a gene with a large estimate is, on average,
a gene with a large error. Such an SE is no longer the sampling SD of the
log fold change, and it is the counterpart for the SE of the thresholding
rule that the memo excludes for the log fold change. The gate examines
only the slope of the log fold change, which `gap_trend` leaves unchanged.

Experiment 30 confirmed the mechanism: the same gap computed on the
regression's residuals, which do not contain the arm effect, scored
`r fmt(.experiment(30, "score"))`. Experiment 31 then replaced the kept
covariate by one that is invariant to the arm effect, and the covariate of
`donor_wls` gives a ratio of `r fmt(validity_df$se_ratio[3], 2)` and a
correlation of `r fmt(validity_df$spearman[3], 2)`.

::: {.takeaway}
On this bank the score pays `r fmt(-sum(withdrawn_df$delta), 3)` nats for
an SE that depends on the estimated log fold change, and the gate on
`slope_weak` does not detect it. The two commits were withdrawn by hand. A
second gate, on the correlation between the reported SE and
$|\widehat\beta_g|$ or on the SE ratio of Table 5, would let the keep rule
refuse such a commit.
:::

# What did not help

::: {.reuse}
The bank of Section 2, dev split. The change is against the best commit at
the time, and positive is worse.
:::

```{r discarded_table}
discarded_df <- discarded_df[order(discarded_df$direction,
                                   discarded_df$experiment), ]
knitr::kable(.experiment_table(discarded_df, sign = 1), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("#", "Commit", "Direction", "Idea",
                           "Change (paired SE)", "Where it lost"),
             align = "llllrl",
             caption = "Table 6. Every discarded commit, grouped by direction, dev split.")
```

```{r direction_table}
direction_vec <- sort(unique(experiment_df$direction))
direction_df <- data.frame(
  direction = direction_vec,
  tried = vapply(direction_vec, function(direction){
    sum(experiment_df$direction == direction)
  }, numeric(1)),
  kept = vapply(direction_vec, function(direction){
    sum(kept_df$direction == direction)
  }, numeric(1)),
  gain = vapply(direction_vec, function(direction){
    fmt(-sum(kept_df$delta[kept_df$direction == direction]))
  }, character(1)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(direction_df, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Direction", "Experiments", "Kept",
                           "Summed gain of the kept (nats)"),
             align = "lrrr",
             caption = "Table 7. Experiments and kept gain per direction, dev split, without the two withdrawn commits.")
```

The bank rewards D1, D2 and D4. The two D5 commits that were kept cancel
each other (Section 4), and the three largest D5 losses share a cause: the
fit's case-control coefficient (experiment 11), its low-rank term
(experiment 18) and its nuisance rate (experiment 24) are estimated at the
level of cells, so they either weight donors by their cell count or absorb
donor effects that the error of the log fold change still contains.
Weighting donors by cell count directly (experiment 10) lost
`r fmt(.experiment(10, "delta"), 3)` nats for the same reason.

On D3 the empirical null's mean is needed, since removing the centring
(experiment 19) lost `r fmt(.experiment(19, "delta"), 3)` nats, and none of
four alternatives to the kept estimator of the centre improved on it. The
SD of the empirical null could not be dropped before the design factor
existed (experiments 1 and 6) and was dropped with it at experiment 7. The
eighth item of the memo's queue, a null SD fitted separately for capped and
estimated genes, was therefore not run.

::: {.takeaway}
Quantities that eSVD-DE estimates at the level of cells did not improve a
donor-level log fold change or its SE on this bank. `donor_wls` reads the
counts, the design and the fitted library, and the fitted library is the
only part of the fit it uses.
:::

# Constants

The truth was not on trial in this run. The kept commits introduced four
numeric constants, and the dev split chose the value of none of them.

| Constant | Where | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1/2 | half count in $l_{dg}$ (step 1) | continuity correction of a Poisson count, which keeps the logarithm finite at a zero count |
| 0 | floor of $\tau^2$ and $\phi$ (step 4) | a variance component is not negative |
| 50 | iteration cap of the trigamma inverse (step 6) | Newton's method converges in under 10 steps, and the cap prevents an endless loop |
| $10^{-8}$ | convergence tolerance of the trigamma inverse (step 6) | single precision in the relative step |

The smoothness of the spline in step 6 is chosen by generalized
cross-validation within each cohort.

# Recommendation

Three statements follow from the evidence of this bank. `donor_wls` is the
best rule the run found, and its gain holds on held-out examples (Section
3). The SD of the empirical null is not needed once the donor-level
covariates are charged through the regression (Section 4). A gate on the
dependence of the SE on the estimate is needed before another run (Section
5).

Three decisions are choices that the evidence does not settle, and they are
Kevin's: whether the withdrawal of `gap_trend` stands, whether the branch
`autoresearch_lfcse/nov11` is merged, and whether `donor_wls` replaces the
earlier recommendation for `compute_log_fold_change()` before it has been
checked on a second bank and on the real cohorts.

::: {.recipe}
For one cohort fitted by `eSVD()` with the fitted library kept:

1. **Inputs.** The counts, the fitted library `library_mat`, the design
   matrix, the donor of each cell and the arm of each cell.
2. **Check.** Each arm has at least 5 donors, and $n - q \ge 1$ after the
   donor-level covariates enter $D$. The bank does not cover fewer than 5
   donors per arm.
3. **Fit.** `report_lfc_se(view)` of `RULE_nov11_claude.R`, which is
   `donor_wls` (Section 1.3, steps 1 to 8).
4. **Output.** `log2fc` and `se` per gene. The Wald statistic is
   `log2fc / se`, referred to the standard normal distribution.
5. **Report alongside.** The mean $\delta_0$ of the empirical null and the
   shift $\delta_0 \cdot \text{median}_g\, s_g$, the fitted $\tau^2$ and
   $\phi$, the prior degrees of freedom $\nu_0$, and the Spearman
   correlation between `se` and the absolute `log2fc`.
6. **When to fall back.** If that correlation is far from zero, or if the
   two arms differ visibly in the spread of their log donor means, the
   log fold change of `donor_wls` is a contrast of geometric means that
   need not equal the log ratio of mean expression (Section 9), and
   `raw_null` is reported beside it.
:::

**Three next experiments.**

1. *An estimand check for the log-scale log fold change (D1; a new bank
   factor).* The difference of mean log donor means equals the log ratio of
   mean expression only when the two arms have the same donor variance,
   which the bank imposes. A bank with unequal donor SD between the arms
   would show whether the gain of experiment 12 survives, or whether a
   correction of half the difference of the arms' log-scale variances is
   needed.
2. *Donor-level depth error (D2; a new bank factor).* The donor offset of
   step 3 is at one paired SE here because the bank's donors carry no
   common depth error. A factor for that error would test the offset and
   whether the SE should then exclude that component.
3. *Capped genes (D5; a new bank).* The bank caps 13% of genes at the wide
   rate range against 73% in the Velmeshev cohort, and the capped genes
   score `r fmt(.block("score_status_capped", "test", "donor_wls"), 3)` on
   test against `r fmt(.block("score_status_capped", "dev", "donor_wls"), 3)`
   on dev. `donor_wls` no longer reads the nuisance rate, so the question
   is whether its SE stays calibrated when most genes are capped.

# What we glossed over

- **The estimand.** The log fold change of `donor_wls` is a contrast of
  geometric means over donors. It is taken up by the first next experiment
  of Section 8.
- **How much of eSVD-DE the rule needs.** The contribution of the fitted
  library was not isolated, and the bank cannot reward the embedding
  (Section 1.3.2). A run of `donor_wls` with a plain library size, and a
  bank factor that confounds cell state with the arm, would settle both.
- **The package's p-value** was not on trial and still uses the posterior,
  so it can disagree with the Wald statistic of `donor_wls` (Section
  1.3.2).
- **Keeps at one paired SE.** Experiments 9, 27 and 31 cannot be separated
  from noise individually, and the test split scored only the final rule. A
  second bank (Section 8) would test the donor offset.
- **The SE diagnostics of Table 5** rest on 12 dev cohorts and a script
  that was not kept. The proposed gate (Section 5) would compute them for
  every example.
- **`k_err` and `r_err`**, the errors in the two moments of Was2CoDE's
  Figure 4, are omitted from Table 1. They are defined for about 80% of
  pairs and are dominated by a few near-zero denominators (`BANK.md`), so
  they are read by stratum in `csv/RUN_nov11/scores.csv`.
- **Real cohorts.** No real cohort was read in this run. The exploration
  of 2026-11-07 (`additional_context/2026-11-07_std-exploration/`) holds
  the real-data checks that `donor_wls` has not yet been through.
- **The trial file's header.** The header comment of
  `report_rule_claude.R` at the best commit describes the rule as of
  experiment 15. The file was left as scored, and the header of
  `RULE_nov11_claude.R` is the accurate description.

# Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `notes/RULE_nov11_claude.R` | `donor_wls`, self-contained; mirrors the best commit |
| `notes/RUN_nov11_claude.md` | the run report in the protocol's format |
| `notes/MEMO_claude.md`, `notes/BANK.md` | the agreed design and the bank as built |
| `diagnostics/export_run_nov11_claude.R` | writes `notes/csv/RUN_nov11/` from the scorer's untracked `output/` |
| `diagnostics/plot_run_nov11_claude.R` | writes the four figures of `notes/figures/RUN_nov11/` from `output/` |
| `csv/RUN_nov11/results.csv` | one row per logged commit, the baseline first: the columns of the log, the experiment number and the change against the best at the time |
| `csv/RUN_nov11/experiments.csv` | one row per experiment: direction, idea, paired SE, strata that moved |
| `csv/RUN_nov11/scores.csv` | one row per example, split and rule (`raw_null`, `donor_wls`): the score and the diagnostics of that example |
| `csv/RUN_nov11/blocks.csv` | one row per line of a summary block, per split and rule |
| `csv/RUN_nov11/validity.csv` | one row per rule of Table 5 |

**Reproducibility.** The bank is `lfcse-bank-1`, with
`r paired_list$dev$num_examples` dev and `r paired_list$test$num_examples`
test rows in its manifests, and the scorer's budget is
`r fmt(.block("budget", "dev", "donor_wls"), 0)` seconds on 8 cores. The
harness is as of commit `r paste0("\x60", results_df$commit[1], "\x60")`
and did not change during the run. The best commit is rescored by
`git checkout `r best_commit` && Rscript autoresearch_lfcse/harness/evaluate_claude.R dev`,
and both diagnostics scripts are run from the repository root with
`Rscript`.
